goal: One picture of the six family members in one row that shows the word family: Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, Tom, and Lily stand together and smile.
mustShow: Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, Tom, and Lily

colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows Mom, picture 2 shows Dad, picture 3 shows Grandma, picture 4 shows Grandpa, picture 5 shows the boy Tom, and picture 6 shows the girl Lily. Each picture holds a front view and a three-quarter view: copy only the named person from each picture and ignore its white background. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions (a big head and a small body); the adults have adult proportions, about one and a half times as tall as the five-year-old children, and Tom, who is eight, is a little taller than Lily. The hands are small, clean hands with five clear short fingers and a thumb when open, never fists. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; no character here has an eyelash flick. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. Do not change anyone's skin tone, hair, or clothes. The picture: the six family members stand together in one straight row on the same ground, all facing the camera and smiling, all six full body in view from head to feet, from left to right Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, Tom, and Lily. A square card picture on a plain pure white background: the row is at the middle of the square, with a wide empty white margin on every side. Count them: six people, each with a clear, whole, friendly face. Exactly six people: no other person, no animal, and nothing else in the picture. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Mom: a woman of about thirty-five with wavy shoulder-length dark-brown hair with a side parting, a coral-pink long-sleeved blouse with a collar, blue jeans, white sneakers. Dad: a man of about thirty-eight with short dark-brown hair with a side parting, a mustard-yellow polo shirt, dark-blue jeans, brown shoes. Grandma: an older woman, a little shorter than Mom, with short curly silver-gray hair, a rose-red cardigan over a cream blouse, a long dark-blue skirt, brown flat shoes. Grandpa: an older man, a little shorter than Dad, with short white hair and a small white mustache, a green knitted cardigan over a white shirt, brown trousers, brown shoes. Tom: a boy of eight with the same chibi proportions as a five-year-old child (a huge round head, about half of his height, no neck, a short chubby body), only a little taller, with short dark-brown hair swept to the side, big brown eyes, a plain navy-blue T-shirt (no stripes), khaki shorts, red shoes. Lily: a girl of five with a short dark-brown bob with a straight fringe and one small lilac bow at the side of her hair, big brown eyes, a lilac dress with short sleeves and a small white collar, white socks, pink shoes. The page text is "family" and is context only: do not draw any text. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos. The picture is for young children and is rated G.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture of six people. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: very thick, bold, even black lines (about five times a normal outline), like a coloring book for very young children, simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw fewer, larger inner shapes: leave out small folds, seams, pocket lines, and buttons. The lines stay equally thick everywhere, also on the face and the hands. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw each mouth exactly as in picture 1. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, and the cuffs. Mom's hair is one closed shape. Her blouse, jeans, and each sneaker are closed shapes. Dad's hair is one closed shape. His polo shirt, jeans, and each shoe are closed shapes. Grandma's curly hair is one closed cloud-like shape with no strands. Her cardigan, blouse, skirt, and each shoe are closed shapes. Grandpa's hair is one closed shape and his mustache is one closed shape. His cardigan, shirt, trousers, and each shoe are closed shapes. Tom's hair is one closed shape. His plain T-shirt (no stripes), each pocket of the shorts, and each shoe are closed shapes. Lily's bob and her one small bow are closed shapes. Her dress, collar, socks, and each shoe are closed shapes. Draw exactly six people: Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, Tom, and Lily, in one row, all full body and in view. Use the thickest lines that keep each face readable: about eight times a normal outline. For each of the six persons draw only the hair, the face, the top, the bottoms, and the shoes as closed shapes; Grandma's and Grandpa's cardigans stay as closed shapes; no collar, cuff, button, or pocket lines. Each face has two eyes with solid black pupils and one smile curve. Grandpa's glasses are two simple circles. Each face has only two eyes (each a closed outline with a big solid black pupil) and one smile curve: no nose line, no eyebrows, and no inner ear lines. Each hand is one small closed rounded shape. Every outline is one closed line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Draw only the six people: no ground line, no shadow, and no background shapes. Do not draw any text, letters, or numbers.
